prose_updates.tldr: The note solves the unrestricted compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint game, constructs face-complete least-favorable priors, proves convergence of primal--dual exchange bounds without a complexity-rate claim, and gives a finite sufficient certificate for the no-one-index branch: exact saddle closure for a finite endpoint prior together with a nonvanishing analytic score and one regular curved score-zero arc implies a unique minimax rule outside every measurable one-index class. The asymmetric triangular example has value \(2/3\) and proves coexistence of one-index and non-one-index optima. The requested fully rational unbalanced curved-score witness remains unresolved: an explicit rational attempt has curved boundary \(3\cosh z_1=2\cosh z_2\), but exact inequalities rule it out because \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\). The finite all-one-index, coexistence, or no-one-index primitive criterion also remains open. Conditional feasible transfer uses reverse deficiency only for its lower bound and a separate joint total-variation premise for its upper bound; it makes no sample-splitting derivation or rate claim.

project_justification.gap: Theorem 3 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} is the feasible fully differentiable result. Its Assumption 5(i) imposes convexity and centrosymmetry for directionally differentiable bounds, Theorem 4 supplies selected rules for that limit game, Theorem 5 gives their feasible transfer, and the Conclusion leaves the joint directional-differentiability and non-centrosymmetry regime open. \cite{Yata2025Optimal} relies on an antipodal modulus pair. \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision} imposes open-set sign ambiguity and establishes multiplicity without classifying the full unrestricted correspondence; the present primitive class instead uses pointwise sign ambiguity. The remaining gap here is constructive and exact: neither the verified sources nor the frozen core supply a rational unbalanced least-favorable endpoint prior with a globally certified curved Bayes boundary.
project_justification.niche: Finite endpoint priors produce analytic differences of Gaussian mixtures. Their global primal--dual gap and local boundary jets are finite objects that can certify properties of the entire unrestricted minimax correspondence, including failure of every scalar-index representation. Exact rational closure is materially stronger than numerical candidate-prior search because every charged support risk must equal one common value.
project_justification.fill: The project derives unrestricted saddle duality and face-complete dual representatives, proves a convergent exchange certificate without a complexity rate, and proves that exact finite-prior saddle closure plus a nonvanishing curved Bayes-score boundary yields uniqueness and the no-one-index category. It also gives the value-\(2/3\) triangular coexistence regression test. A fully rational unbalanced instance satisfying the curved-score certificate is not claimed: the explicit rational curved attempt recorded this round fails the exact dual lower bound, and the complete primitive trichotomy remains answer-open.

sampling_model.design: The canonical experiment is one observation \(Z_h\sim N(h,\Sigma)\). In the conditional transfer result, the reverse-deficiency condition \(\sup_{h\in H}\lVert L_nN(h,\Sigma)-P_{n,h}\rVert_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\) is used only for the minimax lower bound. The feasible upper bound is conditional on a separate joint total-variation approximation; no two-sided experiment equivalence is asserted or needed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: A training sample may be used to construct \(\widehat{\mathsf G}_n\), including \(\widehat\Sigma_n\), but legal membership in \(\mathcal G_p\) and the numerical \(\mathsf B_\kappa\) bounds are separate assumptions. On the common legal event, a deterministic measurable tie-breaking premise for the finite-tolerance certified selector is required, and every finite tolerance \(\varepsilon_n\) is strictly positive. The feasible upper bound additionally assumes joint total-variation approximation of \((\widehat Z_n,\widehat{\mathsf G}_n)\) by the Gaussian reference law. Sample splitting is not claimed to derive that premise, and no convergence rate is attached.

prose_updates.related_work: Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Decision}, establish multiplicity and qualified failure of linear threshold rules in partially identified treatment choice, but do not exclude every randomized measurable rule based on one linear projection. Montiel Olea, Qiu, and Stoye, \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local}, solve the smooth asymmetric and nonsmooth centrosymmetric regimes separately and leave their joint relaxation open; the present compact asymmetric polyhedral class occupies that orthogonal regime, not a superclass of their full Assumption-5 class. Yata, \cite{Yata2025Optimal}, obtains an optimal one-index rule from an antipodal modulus pair under centrosymmetry. Tetenov, \cite{Tetenov2012Asymmetric}, derives threshold structure for point-identified asymmetric regret, showing that asymmetry alone does not yield the present non-index conclusion. Aradillas Fern\'andez et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025LeastFavorable}, provide a numerical stochastic-mirror-descent method for locating approximate least-favorable distributions and nearly optimal tests; that method can supply candidate priors but does not furnish the exact global rational interval certificate required here. Aradillas Fern\'andez et al., \cite{AradillasFernandezEtAl2025Epsilon}, optimize mixtures over a fixed finite rule menu, whereas the present saddle ranges over all measurable randomized rules. Teicher, \cite{Teicher1963Mixtures}, supplies finite-normal-mixture identifiability, and Zahm et al., \cite{ZahmEtAl2020Ridge}, study measurable ridge functions and gradient diagnostics; neither source proves the exact endpoint-game saddle certificate posed here. Hirano and Porter, \cite{HiranoPorter2009}, provide limit-experiment motivation only; the secondary feasible result is explicitly conditional on reverse deficiency for the lower bound and a separate joint total-variation premise for the upper bound.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The curved-score theorem is a sufficient certificate, not a completed unbalanced example or a necessary-and-sufficient normal-fan classification. Its exact global premise cannot be replaced by a plot, a sampled grid, or a floating-point optimizer gap. With rational primitives and rational \(q\), complementary slackness forces exact rational Gaussian decision probabilities at every charged support point; the current core contains no non-collinear mixture for which those equalities are certified. The value-\(2/3\) triangular witness establishes coexistence only. Exchange iterates use exact restricted-game and worst-state oracles, make no complexity-rate claim, and use strictly positive finite tolerances. Conditional transfer separately assumes reverse deficiency, legal bounded game estimation, selector measurability, and joint total-variation approximation.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved frontier is exact saddle geometry for compact polyhedral Gaussian endpoint games: complete unrestricted duality, face-complete priors, the triangular coexistence witness, convergent primal--dual bounds without a complexity rate, and a finite sufficient curved-score theorem for the no-one-index branch. A rational unbalanced instance satisfying that theorem has not been certified; the explicit rational curved attempt is rejected by the exact gap \(b(\pi)\leq1/3<3/7\leq v\). The full primitive trichotomy remains open. The centered antipodal specialization and the compact-polyhedral overlap with Theorem 4 of \cite{MontielOleaQiuStoye2026Local} are comparators only. Conditional feasible transfer is secondary, has no named-model instantiation or rate claim, and retains strictly positive finite certificate tolerances.

statement_notes.justification: This remains the early kill test for the no-one-index branch. The explicit rational attempt shows that unbalanced masses and a curved Gaussian-mixture boundary are easy to obtain separately, but exact least-favorability fails and cannot be repaired by numerical precision alone.
statement_notes.gap: The unresolved step is an exact non-collinear rational equalizer: rational saddle value and endpoint data force rational Gaussian decision probabilities at every charged support point, while no verified source or frozen record supplies the required symmetry, interval certificate, or impossibility theorem.
statement_notes.consumer: A successful certificate would prove that genuinely multivariate reporting is sometimes unavoidable; a general impossibility theorem would sharply simplify the classification program. The failed square candidate prevents software from mistaking a curved approximate Bayes boundary for exact minimax closure.
